item.title: Happy National Drive Electric Week!
item.description:
Happy National Drive Electric Week!

National Drive Electric Week, Sep 22-Oct 1, 2023, is a nationwide celebration to raise awareness of the many benefits of all-electric and plug-in hybrid cars, trucks, motorcycles, and more. In Columbus pollution from transportation and traditional vehicles contributes the most amount of emissions toward climate change. Moving to electric and zero emissions vehicles will reduce pollution and help ensure a healthy community now and in the future. Last week Councilmember Emmanuel Remy, Environment Committee Chair, recognized Drive Electric Columbus with a Resolution around their efforts to encourage electric vehicle adoption. Be sure to attend their National Drive Electric Week event on Sept. 30th at BrewDog Dog Tap!

Columbus Region Green Fund Launches

On September 12, Mayor Andrew J. Ginther joined partners at Corban Commons Senior Living to celebrate and officially kick-off the Columbus Region Green Fund (CRGF). As an independent non-profit, the CRGF will act as an innovative financial hub supporting an equitable clean energy transition. Its first financial product, known as the Impact Solar model, will use the City’s $7 million investment to support 75 non-profits and affordable housing developments with onsite solar projects. Corban Commons Senior Living will be the first project supported by the CRGF.

Staff Spotlight

Name: Mikhail Yahtnitskiy

Title: Regulatory Compliance Advisor

About Me: I’m an environmental professional who loves to help companies and institutions understand and meet their regulatory needs while working towards a more sustainable future. I got my Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science from The Ohio State University and am currently pursuing my Masters in Sustainability Leadership from Arizona State University.   I started out my career in the private sector and am now excited to help spearhead the changes happening within our own City. I’m a collector of hobbies and try to spend as much time outdoors as possible.

Columbus Receives ‘Gold Status’ E3C Award from Ohio EPA

This month, the City of Columbus was recognized by the Ohio EPA for Encouraging Environmental Excellence (E3C) and given a Gold level award - the highest achievement possible! The award recognizes the City’s excellence in environmental compliance, climate and sustainability policies, and programs. Councilmember Emmanuel Remy, Environment Committee Chair, and Public Utilities Director Kristen Atha joined leadership from Sustainable Columbus to accept the award from Ohio EPA Director Anne Vogel on behalf of the City.

‘Cash In on Clean Energy Tour’ coming to Columbus!

Hosted by America Is All In, the “Cash In on Clean Energy Tour” is a series of monthly, in-person events that will take place in cities around the country from July 2023 to October 2023 and the third stop is right here in Columbus! This event will feature an expert-led workshop for business, government and non-profit community leaders to learn how to utilize the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). Experts will be on-site to answer questions and provide information about direct pay and tax credits as well as specific clean electricity, buildings, and transportation incentives. RSVP now for this FREE Columbus event on Tuesday, October 10 from 1:00-6:00pm.

item.title: Climate Pollution Reduction - Take the Survey!
item.description:
Dear Neighbors,

Sustainable Columbus is taking our climate action planning to new heights, and we need your input! The Climate Pollution Reduction Grant (CPRG) is an Environmental Protection Agency program that supports communities tackling climate change and air pollution. This planning grant offers funds to create strategies for reducing greenhouse gasses and other identified pollutants. Sustainable Columbus, in partnership with the Mid-Ohio Regional Planning Commission (MORPC), Power A Clean Future Ohio (PCFO), IMPACT Community Action, and The Ohio State University, has received $1 million to support these efforts in the Central Ohio region. This planning effort will cover 10 counties: Franklin, Delaware, Licking, Fairfield, Union, Pickaway, Madison, Perry, Morrow, and Hocking counties. Our focus is on regional climate action, with a special emphasis on benefiting low-income and disadvantaged communities, in line with federal Justice40 goals.

The CPRG program has two phases. The first planning phase requires both a Priority Climate Action Plan, due March 1, 2024, and a Comprehensive Climate Action Plan, due two years after the planning grant award, in July 2025. The work for the grant’s Comprehensive Climate Action Plan will support the 2025 update of the Columbus Climate Action Plan (2021). A second phase of implementation grants through the CPRG will be available on a competitive basis for all entities who completed a Priority Climate Action Plan, with a total of $4.6 billion allocated nationwide for climate action implementation programs. 

As we begin this planning process, we need your input on how best to involve you as community members throughout the project. Please take this survey to help guide our communication and engagement efforts over the next two planning years.

Bethany Bella
Climate Pollution Reduction Coordinator

item.title: Beat the Heat this Summer!
item.description:
Beat the Heat this Summer!

Today the Federal government launches a mid-season Heat Safety Awareness campaign to raise awareness around extreme heat, and how to prepare for and prevent heat-related illness and death. Rising temperatures and extreme heat are one of Columbus’ biggest climate risks. That’s why our Columbus Climate Action Plan includes strategies like increasing tree canopy, creating a network of resilience hubs and ensuring climate risks, (like extreme heat) are  part of our regional emergency alert systems. Locally, Franklin County and its jurisdictions have been hard at work to update their Hazard Mitigation Plan and we’ve been participating to ensure climate hazards are front and center! The plan is now ready for public review, and the County is asking residents and stakeholders to review the draft plan and provide feedback. The Public Review Period is open until August 11th. Click here to review the plan: https://www.franklincountyohhmp.com/

Climate Pollution Reduction Grant

Sustainable Columbus, along with our partners MORPC, PCFO, IMPACT Community Action, and The Ohio State University, applied for $1 million through the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) Climate Pollution Reduction Grant (CPRG) opportunity available as part of the Inflation Reduction Act. This planning grant will support climate action planning efforts across the Columbus Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA), and serve as an update to the previously planned 2025 update of the Columbus Climate Action Plan. Participating in this planning grant also ensures eligibility for EPA’s Phase 2 of nearly $4.6 billion in competitive implementation funds. Funding for this first phase of the CPRG is expected to be awarded by August 2023, and work has already begun to ensure coordination and collaboration across all partners in this 10-county planning process.

item.title: Celebrating National Bike Month!
item.description:
Celebrating National Bike Month!

May is National Bike Month and National Bike to Work Day is this Friday! Supporting active, pollution free transportation such as biking and walking is part of the Columbus Climate Action Plan, and this month is all about raising awareness around the many benefits of biking. To increase awareness and showcase bike opportunities all around us, the Mid-Ohio Regional Planning Commission (MORPC) will be hosting two events to celebrate National Bike to Work Day this Friday, May 19th. Learn more about the morning bike ride and register to attend here or head to Understory for an evening Happy Hour from 4pm – 6pm!

Columbus Breaks Ground on Two Solar Projects

On May 4th, Mayor Andrew J. Ginther stood with members of the Department of Public Utilities, NextEra Energy and the Ohio Environmental Council to announce 45 MW of new, clean energy solar projects for the City of Columbus. The Parsons (27MW) and Jackson Pike (18 MW) Solar projects will power nearly 7,500 homes served by the City’s Division of Power, and bring their clean energy provision up to 60%. The Jackson Pike project is being developed on a former landfill site, bringing a brownfield site back into productive use. These projects support action 7.2 to Increase Commercial Onsite Solar in the Columbus Climate Action Plan, and the specific target of reaching 200 MW of municipal solar by 2030!

item.title: 2023 Solar Co-Op Launch
item.description:
For Immediate Release

April 19, 2023

 

Contact:

Erin Beck, Assistant Director, 614-645-3522, ebbeck@columbus.gov

New 2023 Solar Co-Op to Help Columbus Families Go Solar

Columbus, OH – The City of Columbus is partnering with nonprofit Solar United Neighbors to launch its third Columbus Area Solar Co-Op, an opportunity for Columbus-area homeowners to learn about solar energy and have a system installed on their homes while supporting Columbus’ climate and equity goals.

"Columbus is proud to continue our partnership with Solar United Neighbors to help residents understand and realize the benefits of going solar,” said City of Columbus Mayor Andrew J. Ginther. "Equitably transitioning to clean energy sources is critical to the Columbus Climate Action Plan, and this co-op is helping our community reach our goal of becoming carbon neutral by 2050."

The co-op is free for residents to join, and joining is not a commitment to purchase a system. Once the group is large enough, Solar United Neighbors will submit a request for proposals to local solar installers. The chosen installer will then develop individualized proposals for each co-op member. After that time, members can decide if going solar is right for them.

“Solar electricity is good for everyone.”," said Mryia Williams, Ohio Program Associate for Solar United Neighbors. "Our solar co-op makes it easy for members to feel comfortable with their decision to go solar by helping them get a better deal on installation, providing unbiased expert guidance, and ensuring the right system for their home."

The nonprofit Solar United Neighbors (SUN) is partnering with Sustainable Columbus, IMPACT Community Action, Green Columbus and MORPC to host the solar co-op opportunity. Solar United Neighbors has hosted two solar co-ops in coordination with the City of Columbus since 2021. Through those efforts, over 350 residents have learned about solar energy, and 54 families now have solar panels because of a solar co-op. These homeowners represent 422.94 kW in total solar installed size and 7,221.2 metric tons of carbon offset.

The 2023 Columbus Area Solar Co-Op, through its partnership with IMPACT Community Action, will again seek to connect the Empowered! clean-energy jobs-training program with the selected installer for mentorship, training and apprenticeship or job opportunities. IMPACT will also host a solar co-op celebration and kickoff event this Thursday, April 19, at 5:30 p.m. to recognize past participants and help other residents learn about the co-op.

“It’s important that we all do our part to make sure we’re doing what we can to better the Earth and environment,” said Ja’net Graham, Senior-Manager Energy Advocacy at IMPACT Community Action. “Participating and showing an interest in the solar co-op is one step that all that of us Columbus residents can take to help combat climate change.”

SUN will host several free information sessions to educate community members about solar energy and the co-op. Individuals interested in going solar can sign up for the co-op or attend one of the upcoming information sessions at www.solarunitedneighbors.org/Columbus.

Informational Solar 101 sessions are scheduled for:

  • Wednesday, April 26, 2023, at 6:00 p.m. online ● Tuesday, May 2, 2023, at 6 p.m. at Hilliard Library (4500 Hickory Chase Way, Hilliard, OH 43206) ● Monday, May 15, 2023, at 5:30 p.m. at Franklinton Library (1061 W. Town St., Columbus, OH 43222)

Sustainable Columbus is the City of Columbus’ sustainability initiative committed to bold action on climate guided by equity and environmental justice. The work is guided by the Columbus Climate Action Plan, the roadmap for the Columbus community to reach carbon neutrality by 2050 and reduce emissions by at least 45% by 2030. Sustainable Columbus seeks to create an equitable, healthy and thriving future for residents in the City of Columbus. To learn more, visit www.Columbus.gov/sustainable.

Solar United Neighbors is a nonprofit organization that works in Ohio and nationwide to represent the needs and interests of solar owners and supporters. Solar co-ops are part of the organization’s mission to create a new energy system with rooftop solar at the cornerstone. Solar United Neighbors holds events and education programs to help people become informed solar consumers, maximize the value of their solar investment, and advocate for fair solar policies.

item.title: Media Release: GreenSpotLight Awards Returns to In Person
item.description:
March 22, 2023

Contact:Erin Beck, Assistant Director, 614-645-3522, ebbeck@columbus.gov

David R. Celebrezze, Resilience & Behavior Change Manager, 614-645-6703, drcelebrezze@columbus.gov

City of Columbus GreenSpotLight Awards Returns to In Person 
Celebration to recognize annual GreenSpot achievements and award businesses for sustainability action


The 2023 City of Columbus’ GreenSpotLight awards celebration event returns in person this Thursday, March 23rd and will recognize three businesses for their outstanding sustainability practices. The large-, medium- and small-organization awards will go to White Castle, MJ Design Associates and Energility, respectively. Members of the GreenSpot Advisory Board selected the three awardees using information provided in the businesses’ GreenSpot annual reports.

“I applaud these award winners and other local businesses for embracing sustainability in their practices, policies and actions,” said City of Columbus Mayor Andrew J. Ginther. “Our community thrives when sustainability is represented as a core value, and we cannot achieve carbon neutrality by 2050 without the full support of all our neighbors.”

These organizations use the MyGreenSpot online tool to adopt and track their sustainability successes in water and energy conservation, waste reduction, green transportation and educational outreach. Actions taken by award winners include installing energy efficient LEDs and motion sensor lighting systems to save energy, installation of low-flow plumbing fixtures to reduce water usage, providing EV charging and discounted rates to employees to encourage sustainable mode shift, and providing workplace recycling and composting efforts.

“We are honored to receive the GreenSpotLight award and it’s gratifying to have our LEED certified Gold Columbus Home Office recognized,” said Shannon Tolliver, Social Responsibility and Environmental Manager. “White Castle is committed to a sustainable future for all our communities and our team members.  As a family owned business, we take the long view and we will continue to work together for a tomorrow that’s even better than today.”

Columbus City Councilmember Rob Dorans will attend the event to recognize and honor the award recipients.

“As our community continues to grow, it's important for all of us to work towards a cleaner, healthier, and more sustainable Columbus. The GreenSpotLight awardees have demonstrated that sustainability can be part of the core mission of any business,” said Columbus City Council President Pro Tem Rob Dorans, Chair of Council’s Public Utilities Committee.

 The awards will be presented to the businesses at the Grange Audubon Center with the event starting at 5:30pm. This event is free and open to the public however RSVPs are encouraged at GreenSpotLight.eventbrite.com.

 The GreenSpot Program began in 2008 to inspire, educate, and recognize those in the community who are taking steps to protect the environment. More than 23,000 households, community groups and businesses are currently members. Membership forms are available for download at www.ColumbusGreenSpot.org

item.title: Celebrating Women’s History Month and our Earth!
item.description:
Celebrating Women’s History Month and our Earth!

March is Women’s History Month! Did you know women tend to have a smaller carbon footprint than men, constitute 80% of climate refugees, and are more at risk of domestic violence due to climate change? These are just a few reasons why being inclusive of gender is critical to equitably fighting and adapting to climate change. We celebrate and honor the many contributions women have made to the environmental movement and will continue to make into the future as we strive to create a more just and equitable world.

Columbus Receives SolSmart “Gold” Designation

The City of Columbus has been designated a “Gold” community by the national SolSmart Program, recognizing our commitment to making it easier, faster and more affordable for residents and businesses to go solar. Columbus is one of only five communities in Ohio to receive Gold status and actions taken to receive the designation included training permitting and inspection staff on solar photovoltaics (PV), allowing solar in all zoning districts, and streamlining permitting processes. Supported by the Federal Department of Energy, since the launch of SolSmart in 2016 over 450 communities have received SolSmart designation of either Bronze, Silver or Gold.

Staff Spotlight

 

Name: Dr. Katherine ‘Swid’ Swidarski

Title: Climate Action Plan Implementation Manager

About Me: I love to eat and love to travel. I am known to many in Columbus as Safety Swid because of my car-free lifestyle and commitment to walking safely. My best advice to others is “adventure every day”

Join Us! GreenSpotLight Awards

Join the GreenSpot Program, City Councilmember Rob Dorans, and Columbus Public Utilities Director Kristen L. Atha for the in-person GreenSpotLight celebration of our community’s GreenSpot achievements! This annual event (back in person for the first time since 2020!) will recognize 3 GreenSpot businesses for their environmental excellence, provide updates on Sustainable Columbus, provide GreenSpot 2023 action plans – plus trivia, prizes and more! This is a great event to network with like-minded residents and sustainability professionals. Attendance is free but please RSVP here. Questions about the event? Contact Greenspot@Columbus.gov!

Columbus Climate Action Plan: In Focus

Action 2.2 in the Columbus Climate Action Plan is to Increase Annual Sustainable Development Funding, with a target of reaching $250 million average annual Commercial PACE investments by 2030.  Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy, or C-PACE, is a financing tool that supports energy efficient building upgrades through a property tax assessment and is locally administered by the Columbus Region Energy Special Improvement District. To date the program has supported 76 projects totaling $228 million with an annual average energy consumption reduction of 26%. Be sure to share this financing resource with your networks!

Earth Month

April is Earth Month! Events will be happening across the Columbus community to equitably support our Climate Action Plan goals and ensure a healthy, vibrant environment and future. Be sure to check out the Green Columbus website for volunteer opportunities or to host your own volunteer event! Earth Day falls on Saturday, 4/22 and be sure to mark your Calendar for these 2 big events:

Columbus Rec & Parks Earth Day Event – 9am – 12pm at Linden Community Center
Start your day with this City driven event focused on natural resource protection and conservation! Activities will include fishing with ODNR as well as as a demonstration on fish filleting, tree planting, pollinator planting, and other outdoor nature activities like birding and a nature scavenger hunt!

Green Columbus Earth Day Celebration – 12-9pm at Genoa Park
Spend your afternoon at this citywide celebration of all things environment! There will be vendors and children’s activities, live music, food trucks and beverages – fun for the whole family!

item.title: Media Release: Columbus Receives SolSmart "Gold" Designation
item.description:
March 07, 2023

Contact: Erin Beck

Assistant Director

614-645-3522

ebbeck@columbus.gov

City of Columbus Receives SolSmart “Gold” Designation for Advancing Solar Energy Adoption

Columbus, OH – The City of Columbus has received a gold designation from the national SolSmart program for making it faster, easier and more affordable for local homes and businesses to adopt solar energy.

“Promoting equitable and efficient clean-energy strategies is critical to the continued success of the Columbus Climate Action Plan,” said City of Columbus Mayor Andrew J. Ginther. “This SolSmart recognition will help to ensure that we are utilizing best practices to grow the solar industry and reduce carbon emissions right here in Columbus, benefiting both our residents and businesses for generations to come.”

To receive a gold designation, cities and counties must make changes to their processes that reduce the time and money required to install a solar energy system. This includes evaluating local permitting and inspection processes as well as enhancing planning and zoning procedures. SolSmart designees must also develop innovations in community engagement, government operations and solar market development. Communities that take sufficient action are awarded gold, silver or bronze status.

"Achieving this designation is a major win for Columbus residents, the local economy, and the environment. Columbus continues its record of nationally recognized leadership on climate and clean energy adoption. This important designation is another step in transitioning our energy economy and will help spur meaningful progress in the community's collective action on climate change," said Joe Flarida, Executive Director of Power a Clean Future Ohio, a nonpartisan non-profit coalition that works with local leaders to develop and implement proven climate solutions.

Actions taken by Columbus that merit its gold designation include training of inspection and permitting staff on solar photovoltaics(PV), allowing solar panels in all zoning districts, and streamlining permitting processes for small PV systems. Permits for small systems, which support residential onsite solar, are able to be processed and issued in one day, aiding in timely completion of projects.

“As we better understand climate change and other stressors on our electrical grid, I am excited to be able to easily and quickly help customers obtain roof top solar panel systems for their homes”, said Scott Messer, Director of the City’s Building and Zoning Services Department.

SolSmart is led by the Interstate Renewable Energy Council (IREC) and the International City/County Management Association (ICMA), and funded by the U.S. Department of Energy Solar Energy Technologies Office. More than 450 municipalities, counties and regional organizations have achieved SolSmart designation since the program launched in 2016.

item.title: Welcome to Sustainable Columbus!
item.description:
Welcome to Sustainable Columbus!

Welcome to the Sustainable Columbus e-newsletter and email program! We are launching this effort in 2023 as part of our commitment to deepening relationships with community, and providing transparency and accountability through our work. Thank you for being here!

Columbus Makes 'A' List and International Climate Recognition

The Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP) –a global environmental nonprofit dedicated to supporting and advancing local climate action efforts – has recognized Columbus as one of 122 “A List” cities and counties for taking bold leadership on environmental action and transparency, despite various economic challenges occurring around the world. To score an A, local governments must disclose their data, maintain a community-wide emissions inventory, and have published a climate action plan. Nearly 20,000 organizations disclosed data to CDP-ICLEI Track in 2022, including more than 18,700 companies comprising 50% of global market capitalization, and over 1,100 cities, states and regions.

Staff Spotlight

Name: Bethany Bella

Title: Building and Energy Coordinator

About Me: Hello, everyone! I’m a passionate sustainability advocate who envisions a just and vibrant future for all. I position my work at the intersection of community planning and solutions that support both people and the planet. I love reading and collecting books, dancing in my kitchen, and photographing my outdoor adventures. I’m excited to support the equity-centered sustainability efforts grown here in the Columbus region – a place I am proud to call home!

Congratulations to Empowered! Grads

Sustainable Columbus has partnered with IMPACT Community Action to launch Empowered!, a 12-week earn while you learn clean energy and construction jobs training program for young people. The program is focused on communities of color, women, and our Opportunity neighborhoods. In December, the 2nd Cohort graduated in a moving ceremony held at IMPACT – congratulations to these amazing young residents on their achievement! Recruitment is in process for the next Cohort beginning in February 2023. Learn more about the program and how to join here.

Columbus Climate Action Plan: In Focus

Action 6.3 in the Columbus Climate Action Plan is to Evaluate Microgrid and Storage Projects, with a target of implementing 5 microgrid pilot projects by 2030. Toward the end of 2022, the Department of Public Utilities unveiled the first of those 5 pilot projects with the City’s first-ever solar powered microgrid at the Tussing Water Booster Station. Check out this video to learn about the project and how it supports our Columbus Climate Action Plan!

item.title: Special Live-Stream Forum with Mayor Ginther
Help keep our parks and trails healthy and safe
item.description:
Residents Urged to Play Safe, Live Smart to Stay Healthy and Help Keep Columbus’ Parks and Trails Safe

Visiting Columbus Recreation and Park Department’s trails and parks are a great way to maintain your physical and mental health, but it’s important to Play Safe, Live Smart and take steps to use them safely.

Columbus’ trails and parks currently are open during the coronavirus (COVID-19) public health emergency. Our trails and parks are a resource to help residents enjoy the outdoors while engaging in recreation, exercise and education.

“In these times of great disruption, the health and safety of our residents is key. We have the ability to slow the spread of COVID-19 by rigorously practicing social distancing,” said Mayor Andrew J. Ginther. “Encouraging residents to use our trails and parks in a safe way helps prevent exposure and maintains access to these important resources.”

As the City of Columbus takes steps to protect residents and stop the spread of COVID-19, City leaders have carefully weighed the benefits and risks to public health of keeping facilities open.  At this time, the City is committed to keeping parks and trails open as long as it remains safe to do so.

While most residents are practicing social distancing at Columbus’ trails and parks, there are some areas where people are not doing as good of a job, including Antrim Park and the Olentangy Trail.

Play Safe, Life Smart: Practicing Social Distancing at Columbus Trails and Parks

Here are some tips to practice social distancing at Columbus' trails and parks:

Do visit parks and trails with your immediate family and those with whom you’re staying at home.

Do take advantage of opportunities to enjoy the outdoors for recreation, exercise and education.

Do pay attention to signage and barriers that restrict access to equipment, such as playgrounds, tennis courts, disc golf courses and basketball courts.

Do maintain a six-foot distance from others when walking, running and biking. You can do this by letting people know you are passing when you come up from behind and safely stepping off the path to let others pass.

Do NOT use parks or trails if you are exhibiting COVID-19 symptoms.

Do NOT step over or remove any barriers that block access to equipment, facilities and parking lots.

Do NOT play group sports using shared equipment, such as basketball, disc golf and tennis.

Do NOT use any equipment such as picnic tables, playgrounds, and basketball, disc golf and tennis courts. Currently, all recreation equipment is closed.

For additional information about COVID-19, visit Columbus Public Health, Ohio Department of Health or Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Additionally, Ohio residents with specific questions related to COVID-19 can also call 833-4-ASK-ODH (833-427-5634). For a full list of department-related updates and closures, visit ColumbusRecParks.com.

item.title: Columbus Public Health Steps-up Enforcement of Social Distancing and Hygiene for Businesses
item.description:
Beginning today, Columbus Public Health will step up inspections on businesses to assure they are complying with the Ohio Department of Health’s orders for social distancing and basic hygiene to slow the spread of COVID- 19.

“We are at a critical moment in slowing the spread of this highly infectious disease in our community,” said Mayor Andrew J. Ginther. “We have received hundreds of complaints that some businesses are not complying with the Ohio Department of Health’s orders, and we must assure that employees and residents are safe.”

Teams of sanitarians will visit businesses to assess the number of people working, if they are able to work at a safe distance from one another and if soap, water or hand sanitizer are readily available. Those not in compliance will receive a warning letter. A second violation will result in citations and could lead to criminal charges.

“We are pleased that most people and businesses are doing their part to slow the spread of COVID-19 by following the Ohio Department of Health’s orders,” said Dr. Mysheika Roberts, Health Commissioner for Columbus Public Health. “However, we continue to receive complaints from residents that some businesses are not following these orders. We will be sending our teams out to investigate these complaints in order to protect the health and safety of our community.”

Columbus Public Health will not be weighing in on whether a company or workers are essential, only if the place of employment is in compliance with the order. Guidelines for Essential Businesses can be found at corona.ohio.gov. 

“Businesses want to do the right thing, but may not know the full extent of the state’s social distancing and safe hygiene requirements. That’s why educating business owners and the public about how we slow the spread of COVID-19 is so important,” said City Attorney Zach Klein. “Our ‘education first, citation second’ approach allows people to learn about the state’s order while still giving health officials and law enforcement the ability to issue a citation if someone refuses to cooperate.”

item.title: Stay at Home
item.description:
Today, Governor DeWine issued a “Stay at Home” order which requires all Ohioans to stay at home, and limit trips to essential errands only. The order will go into effect Monday at 11:59 p.m.

It is important that we take this order seriously to stop community spread of COVID-19. We are at a critical point in our fight to stop the spread of this virus, and we must follow the governor’s order.

But this order should not cause panic, and I urge the residents of Columbus to act responsibly. You will still have access to the necessities you need to keep the community healthy and safe, including grocery stores, pharmacies and health care.

For government, businesses and nonprofit organizations that will remain open to serve critical needs and provide essential services, this is not business as usual. Employees who can work from home should, and steps should already be in place to allow employees to practice safe social distancing and assure proper sanitation. We should redouble our efforts to ensure steps we've taken to protect our employees are being followed in practice.

For individuals, to the extent you must leave home, follow the advice of public health experts. Limit your movement, practice safe social distancing, and wash your hands.

Finally, while these are challenging times, it is not a time for fear. Instead, we must rely on facts. Our decisions should put the common health and well-being of our community and our families first.

Be patient with one another. Support each other and be kind.

These are times unlike any most of us have ever seen, but together we will get through this and we will emerge stronger, smarter and healthier.

item.title: COVID-19 Resource Page
item.description:
We are in a time of great disruption as we fight to slow the spread of COVID-19 in our community. The drastic measures we have implemented are absolutely necessary for the health and safety of our residents. What we do now will lessen the severity and duration of this infection in Columbus.

But I know that these decisions have also caused many of our residents and businesses to suffer – and it has left others wondering how they can help.

The City has compiled a comprehensive page of resources for human services, businesses, volunteer opportunities and online recreation options. We will keep updating in the coming days and weeks.

These are extraordinary times, but they are temporary. We will emerge on the other side.

Be well. Be flexible. Be kind.

item.title: City of Columbus to Delay April Start of Annual Street Sweeping Program
item.description:
The City of Columbus is delaying the April start of its annual street sweeping program at posted routes to ensure convenience and on-street parking availability for residents during the COVID-19 public health crisis.

City street sweeping normally operates from April through October. Street signs with posted sweeping days alert residents when to move their cars on specified days and times. For now, residents may disregard those on-street parking restrictions. The Department of Public Service, Division of Infrastructure Management, will conduct sweeping on an as-needed basis, but ticketing and towing will not be enforced.

The Department will re-evaluate the suspended service in mid-April to possibly resume the street sweeping program in May, pending further developments related to the coronavirus emergency.

“The Department of Public Service is focused on the health and safety of our residents as we maintain delivery of essential city services they depend on every day,” said Director Jennifer L. Gallagher. “Services such as trash collection, traffic operations and street maintenance are our priorities for the well-being of our residents.”

The street sweeping delay is one of several actions the city has taken this week to provide flexibility and convenience to residents following public health guidelines to stay at or work from home. These measures include:

  • No ticketing of vehicle owners for failing to register or for displaying expired license plates following Gov. Mike DeWine’s indefinite closure of Ohio Bureau of Motor Vehicles deputy registrar locations.
  • No enforcement for now of the parking code requiring vehicles parked on the street to be moved after 72 hours.
  • Parking ticket appeal hearings are cancelled indefinitely and all fines and penalties are suspended until hearings resume.
  • Some High Street parking meters in the Short North are temporarily converted to 30 minutes to accommodate carryout service and brief pick-up and drop-off at local restaurants and businesses there.

item.title: State of Emergency
item.description:
A few moments ago, I signed a declaration of a State of Emergency for the City of Columbus drafted by City Attorney Zach Klein with the guidance and counsel of City Council President Shannon Hardin and City Auditor Megan Kilgore. This is necessary both for the city to continue to operate and for the protection of our employees and, ultimately, our residents.

74% of our employees work on the frontline: police, fire, public health nurses, utility plant operators, refuse collectors, just to name a few. They will continue to work, and the critical city services delivered by these dedicated men and women will continue.

Starting today, the city’s remaining full-time workforce – approximately 1,300 people – have been asked to remain at home. Many will be able to work remotely.

All full-time city employees will continue to be paid. Part-time employees will be paid for hours they work.

There is no doubt that this is a difficult time. We have little in history to compare it to.

But I believe in this city and the resiliency of its residents.

We can – and will – get through this together.

item.title: Columbus COVID-19 Update: In-Person Bill Payment and Permitting Services Notification
item.description:
Due to the COVID-19 crisis, the City of Columbus is suspending all in person bill payment and permitting services for the Department of Public Utilities, Building and Zoning Services, Recreation and Parks, and Department of Public Service at the 111 Front Street Coleman Government Center and Jerry Hammond Building at 1111 East Broad Street until further notice.    

Department of Public Utilities payment options:

  • Use drop boxes at 111 Front Street or in front of the Public Utilities Complex along Twin Rivers Drive (910 Dublin Road) 
  • On line portal:   https://schedulepayment.com/Columbus
  • Payment by phone or billing questions can be directed to the Customer Service Center 7 am – 3 pm:  614-645-8276
  • Western Union locations in Kroger stores:  https://www.westernunion.com/us/en/pay-bills.html

Department of Public Utilities permitting and Inspections:

  • Email permit info to UtilityPermits@columbus.gov

Building and Zoning Services:

  • Front Counter will be closed at end of business today and will issue no new permits other than online
  • Residential inspections will stop on all occupied buildings
  • Map Room will be closed at end of business today
  • The following boards and commission have suspended their meetings until further notice:

Board of Zoning Adjustment

Columbus Building Commission

Development Commission

General and Home Improvement Contractors Board

Graphics Commission

Sign Erectors Board

Skilled Trades Review Board

Building and Zoning Services operations will continue until further notice:

  • All online activities will remain available
  • Inspections for commercial, multi-family new build, and residential new builds with scheduling occurring online at www.columbus.gov/bzs or by phone (614) 645-8235

Recreation and Parks:

  • Golf 614-645-3375 mrmusser@columbus.gov
  • Sports Office 614-645-3366 crpdsports@columbus.gov
  • Rental Services 614-645-3340 parkrentals@columbus.gov
  • Special Events 614-645-3800 specialevents@columbus.gov

Department of Public Service:

  • The in-person permit counter will be closed at the end of business today and an online, email or phone permitting process will be utilized.
  • Parking tickets can be paid on line www.parkcolumbus.com or call (844) 565-1295
  • Impound Lot customer hours will be 11am-6pm Monday-Saturday and are subject to change.
  • Use the City of Columbus portal https://portal.columbus.gov/permits for permit applications.
  • Contact the permit counter through email at colspermits@columbus.gov or (614) 645-7497 with any issues or concerns.
  • The following will be impacted:

Process and Issuances of Right-of-Way Permits (i.e. Occupancy permit, excavation, permits, Oversize Permits, Food Truck Permits, etc.

City of Columbus specification books 

No Parking Signs for permitted projects.

item.title: Message from Mayor Ginther: Our Equity Agenda
item.description:
Last night, I was honored to give the first State of the City address of my second term. You elected me to continue to move this city forward with shared prosperity and equity, and the plan I laid out will do exactly that.

In short, the State of the City is strong, but in order for Columbus to reach its full potential as America’s Opportunity City, we must grow dynamically and inclusively.

My priorities are birth-to-five, diversity and inclusion, neighborhoods, public safety and health, economic development, affordable housing, innovation and sustainability. But ultimately they are all about equity.

We live in a country that is more segregated than ever, and we continue to live more segregated lives. I know there are divisions right here in Columbus – last night, there was a protest by a few concerned, passionate residents.  In my speech, I addressed some of their issues. While I respect their right to protest, I hope they will also accept the invitation my office has extended to meet and discuss how we can work together. 

Real change is not quick or easy.  It can be messy and frustrating. We need everyone to show up, learn from all voices and be willing to learn and change to close this divide.

I believe our best days are still ahead of us, and I know we will get there together.
